questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
The Mapping Forgotten Botanists initiative preserves and shares information about botanists whose contributions have received limited attention in conventional histories of science.
Ynes Mexia was a Mexican American botanist represented in the initiative’s biographical archive.
Mexia was born in 1870 and died in 1938.
She began collecting plants professionally in her fifties.
Her expeditions throughout Mexico and South America yielded thousands of botanical specimens.
questions.question: The student wants to set up a discussion of Mexia’s career for an audience already familiar with the Mapping Forgotten Botanists initiative. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Although Ynes Mexia did not begin professional botanical collecting until her fifties, her expeditions eventually produced thousands of specimens.
choices.B: Born in 1870 and deceased by 1938, Ynes Mexia traveled throughout Mexico and South America during her botanical career.
choices.C: Among the scientists represented in the initiative’s biographical archive is botanist Ynes Mexia (1870–1938), whose unusually late-starting career would nevertheless become remarkably productive.
choices.D: The Mapping Forgotten Botanists initiative preserves information about historically overlooked botanists so that their contributions will receive greater attention.

choiceExplanations.C: it efficiently connects Mexia to the initiative that the audience already knows while also introducing the central feature of her career that a subsequent discussion could develop: she began unusually late yet became highly productive.
choiceExplanations.A: provides useful information about Mexia’s career but does not connect her to the initiative, making it less effective as a setup for this particular audience.
choiceExplanations.B: gives biographical dates and travel information but does not establish why Mexia is being introduced in connection with the initiative.
choiceExplanations.D: describes the initiative itself without introducing Mexia’s career, even though the audience is already assumed to know about the project.

questions.explanation: it efficiently connects Mexia to the initiative that the audience already knows while also introducing the central feature of her career that a subsequent discussion could develop: she began unusually late yet became highly productive.

questions.passage: Although movable-type printing reached the Ottoman Empire relatively late, Armenian printers in Constantinople rapidly developed a substantial publishing tradition once presses were established there. _____ by the eighteenth century, workshops in the city were producing religious works, dictionaries, histories, and instructional texts for readers across an extensive commercial network.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Nevertheless,
choices.B: Otherwise,
choices.C: By contrast,
choices.D: In fact,

choiceExplanations.B: “Otherwise,” typically introduces an alternative consequence or condition and does not fit the relationship between a claim and evidence supporting it.
choiceExplanations.A: “Nevertheless,” signals a concession or contrast, but the second sentence supports rather than qualifies the first.
choiceExplanations.C: “By contrast,” also indicates opposition, which is absent here.
choiceExplanations.D: This choice, “In fact,” is correct because the second sentence supplies concrete evidence that reinforces the first sentence’s claim that a substantial publishing tradition developed rapidly. The range of works produced and the broad distribution network make that general claim more specific and convincing.

questions.explanation:
Choice B, “In fact,” is correct because the second sentence supplies concrete evidence that reinforces the first sentence’s claim that a substantial publishing tradition developed rapidly. The range of works produced and the broad distribution network make that general claim more specific and convincing.
Choice A, “Nevertheless,” signals a concession or contrast, but the second sentence supports rather than qualifies the first. Choice C, “By contrast,” also indicates opposition, which is absent here. Choice D, “Otherwise,” typically introduces an alternative consequence or condition and does not fit the relationship between a claim and evidence supporting it.

questions.passage: Photographer Frances Benjamin Johnston’s images of Hampton Institute document actual classrooms, workshops, and students, and the photographs are therefore often described primarily as historical records. That description can be useful, but it may also narrow how viewers evaluate Johnston’s work. If audiences assume that the photographs merely preserve scenes that happened to exist in front of the camera, they may overlook her deliberate choices of framing, staging, lighting, and visual emphasis. In an artistic medium where composition and interpretation are central, such an assumption can make the photographs seem _____
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: less aesthetically constructed than they actually are.
choices.B: difficult to connect to identifiable historical institutions.
choices.C: more influential on later documentary photographers than surviving evidence indicates.
choices.D: impossible to distinguish from photographs made without posed subjects.

choiceExplanations.A: The passage warns that treating Johnston’s photographs mainly as straightforward historical records may cause viewers to underestimate the artistic decisions involved in producing them. If people assume the camera simply recorded preexisting reality, they may perceive the photographs as less deliberately constructed than they truly were.
choiceExplanations.B: is unsupported because the passage explicitly identifies Hampton Institute as the setting.
choiceExplanations.C: introduces the issue of Johnston’s influence on later photographers, which the passage never discusses.
choiceExplanations.D: is too extreme and illogical: the passage says that staging is one of Johnston’s artistic choices, not that her photographs cannot be distinguished from unposed photography.

questions.explanation: The passage warns that treating Johnston’s photographs mainly as straightforward historical records may cause viewers to underestimate the artistic decisions involved in producing them. If people assume the camera simply recorded preexisting reality, they may perceive the photographs as less deliberately constructed than they truly were.

questions.passage:
The following text is from Robert Frost’s 1916 poem “An Old Man’s Winter Night.”
All out-of-doors looked darkly in at him
Through the thin frost, almost in separate stars,
That gathers on the pane in empty rooms.
What kept his eyes from giving back the gaze
Was the lamp tilted near them in his hand.
<u>A light he was to no one but himself
Where now he sat, concerned with he knew what,</u>
A quiet light, and then not even that.
questions.question: Which choice best states the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It establishes that the old man is deliberately hiding his lamp from people outside the house.
choices.B: It emphasizes the old man’s isolation by portraying his presence as meaningful only to himself.
choices.C: It suggests that the old man has become increasingly confused about the physical source of the light.
choices.D: It explains why the old man prefers remaining indoors rather than confronting the severe winter weather.

choiceExplanations.A: is incorrect because nothing indicates that he is concealing the lamp.
choiceExplanations.B: The statement that the man is “a light...to no one but himself” underscores how completely alone he is. The image turns the man himself into a faint, private source of light, emphasizing that no one else is present to see or benefit from his existence in that moment.
choiceExplanations.C: mistakes figurative language for literal confusion; the speaker is metaphorically describing the man, not suggesting that he cannot identify the lamp.
choiceExplanations.D: is unsupported because the underlined lines focus on solitude, not on the reason he remains indoors.

questions.explanation: The statement that the man is “a light...to no one but himself” underscores how completely alone he is. The image turns the man himself into a faint, private source of light, emphasizing that no one else is present to see or benefit from his existence in that moment.

questions.passage: With a primary mirror measuring 10.4 meters across, the Gran Telescopio Canarias is among the largest single-aperture optical telescopes in the _____ the Extremely Large Telescope, whose segmented primary mirror is designed to span 39 meters, will be considerably larger.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: world, but,
choices.B: world but,
choices.C: world, but
choices.D: world but

choiceExplanations.A: This choice does not satisfy the evidence, wording, or grammatical requirement established by the question.
choiceExplanations.B: incorrectly places the comma after “but.” Choice C places commas on both sides of “but,” unnecessarily separating the conjunction from the second independent clause.
choiceExplanations.D: omits the comma required before a coordinating conjunction joining two independent clauses.
choiceExplanations.C: The text contains two independent clauses: “the Gran Telescopio Canarias is among the largest single-aperture optical telescopes in the world” and “the Extremely Large Telescope...will be considerably larger.” When two independent clauses are joined by the coordinating conjunction “but,” a comma should appear before the conjunction: “world, but the Extremely Large Telescope....”

questions.explanation: The text contains two independent clauses: “the Gran Telescopio Canarias is among the largest single-aperture optical telescopes in the world” and “the Extremely Large Telescope...will be considerably larger.” When two independent clauses are joined by the coordinating conjunction “but,” a comma should appear before the conjunction: “world, but the Extremely Large Telescope....”

questions.passage: Volcanologists commonly distinguish several broad eruption styles, including Hawaiian, Strombolian, Vulcanian, and Plinian. Mount Stromboli is associated with the _____ repeated bursts of incandescent lava fragments have made that pattern of activity especially characteristic of the volcano.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: Strombolian style, for example;
choices.B: Strombolian style; for example;
choices.C: Strombolian style, for example,
choices.D: Strombolian style; for example,

choiceExplanations.B: incorrectly places a semicolon after “for example,” where a comma is required.
choiceExplanations.A: incorrectly uses a comma before “for example” to connect two independent clauses and then places a semicolon after the transition.
choiceExplanations.C: creates a comma splice because two independent clauses are joined only by a comma and a transitional phrase.
choiceExplanations.D: The sentence contains two independent clauses: “Mount Stromboli is associated with the Strombolian style” and “repeated bursts of incandescent lava fragments have made that pattern of activity especially characteristic of the volcano.” A semicolon can correctly separate those clauses. The transitional phrase “for example” appears at the beginning of the second clause and should be followed by a comma: “style; for example, repeated bursts....”

questions.explanation: The sentence contains two independent clauses: “Mount Stromboli is associated with the Strombolian style” and “repeated bursts of incandescent lava fragments have made that pattern of activity especially characteristic of the volcano.” A semicolon can correctly separate those clauses. The transitional phrase “for example” appears at the beginning of the second clause and should be followed by a comma: “style; for example, repeated bursts....”

questions.passage: Basalt, _____ extensively in road construction, railway ballast, and architectural cladding, is an igneous rock formed when low-viscosity lava cools rapidly at or near Earth’s surface.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: used
choices.B: to use
choices.C: using
choices.D: the use

choiceExplanations.D: “the use,” creates a noun phrase that cannot grammatically modify “Basalt” in this construction.
choiceExplanations.A: This choice, “used,” is correct. The sentence needs a past-participial modifier describing basalt: “Basalt, used extensively in road construction, railway ballast, and architectural cladding, is an igneous rock....” The phrase “used extensively...” functions as a reduced relative clause equivalent to “which is used extensively....”
choiceExplanations.B: “to use,” incorrectly suggests an infinitive purpose construction rather than describing an established application of basalt.
choiceExplanations.C: “using,” would make basalt the agent performing the action of using something; instead, basalt is the material that is used, so the passive participle “used” is required.

questions.explanation:
Choice D, “used,” is correct. The sentence needs a past-participial modifier describing basalt: “Basalt, used extensively in road construction, railway ballast, and architectural cladding, is an igneous rock....” The phrase “used extensively...” functions as a reduced relative clause equivalent to “which is used extensively....”
Choice A, “the use,” creates a noun phrase that cannot grammatically modify “Basalt” in this construction. Choice B, “to use,” incorrectly suggests an infinitive purpose construction rather than describing an established application of basalt. Choice C, “using,” would make basalt the agent performing the action of using something; instead, basalt is the material that is used, so the passive participle “used” is required.

questions.passage:
The following text is from Lenora Whitcomb’s 1912 poem “Estuary at Dusk.”
The tide withdraws; along the sand
A violet gleam and seawater blend,
Until no watching eye can tell
Where one begins or one may end.
So quietly the colors merge,
So slight the change from gray to blue,
The keenest sight could scarcely resolve
The boundary passing through.
questions.question: As used in the text, what does the word “resolve” most nearly mean?

choices.A: settle
choices.B: distinguish
choices.C: explain
choices.D: transform

choiceExplanations.B: The speaker describes two colors blending so gradually that even “the keenest sight” can barely perceive the boundary between them. In this context, “resolve” means to distinguish or perceive separately, so B is correct.
choiceExplanations.A: “settle,” reflects another common meaning of resolve, as in resolving a dispute, but no disagreement is being settled here.
choiceExplanations.C: “explain,” can also be associated with resolving a problem, but the passage concerns visual perception rather than explanation.
choiceExplanations.D: “transform,” does not fit the idea that an observer is trying to detect a nearly invisible boundary.

questions.explanation: The speaker describes two colors blending so gradually that even “the keenest sight” can barely perceive the boundary between them. In this context, “resolve” means to distinguish or perceive separately, so B is correct.

questions.passage: Marine ecologists seeking inspiration for artificial-reef designs sometimes examine photographs of exceptionally complex coral formations. A photograph, however, fixes one viewpoint and one instant; it cannot reveal how fish move through passages at different depths, how currents redirect around projecting structures, or how neighboring organisms alter the use of the same space over time. A photograph of a reef formation therefore ______
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: tends to overstate the ecological significance of organisms positioned near the camera.
choices.B: inaccurately represents how the reef would appear to an observer unfamiliar with marine environments.
choices.C: cannot fully convey the spatial and ecological effects of the formation’s three-dimensional structure.
choices.D: conceals gradual chemical changes occurring within the reef’s mineral framework.

choiceExplanations.B: shifts the issue to how an inexperienced observer would interpret the image, whereas the passage focuses on information that the photograph itself cannot capture.
choiceExplanations.A: introduces a specific distortion involving organisms close to the camera, but the passage never discusses this effect.
choiceExplanations.C: The passage emphasizes limitations inherent in a static, two-dimensional photograph: it cannot show movement through different depths, changing currents, or interactions that vary over time. Therefore, the photograph cannot fully convey the effects of the reef’s three-dimensional structure, making this choice correct.
choiceExplanations.D: concerns chemical changes in reef material, a topic not mentioned in the passage.

questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes limitations inherent in a static, two-dimensional photograph: it cannot show movement through different depths, changing currents, or interactions that vary over time. Therefore, the photograph cannot fully convey the effects of the reef’s three-dimensional structure, making B correct.

questions.passage: In a study by urban sociologist Amina Kader, Luís Mendonça, and colleagues, residents of Rotterdam, Netherlands, and Valparaíso, Chile, were surveyed about their use of neighborhood public libraries. Of 1,216 respondents in Rotterdam, 52.1% reported visiting a library at least monthly; among 1,004 respondents in Valparaíso, the corresponding figure was 39.6%. <u>The difference might initially appear to result simply from unequal access to library branches.</u> Yet 71% of Valparaíso respondents reported living within a fifteen-minute walk of a branch, compared with only 58% of Rotterdam respondents, so proximity alone cannot account for the higher reported use in Rotterdam.
questions.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It marks a shift from reporting the researchers’ interpretation of the data to describing the procedures they used to collect those data.
choices.B: It supplies background information necessary to understand how the researchers selected participants for the survey.
choices.C: It introduces a contrasting case that demonstrates why the researchers’ original conclusion should be rejected.
choices.D: It proposes a possible explanation for the researchers’ findings that subsequent evidence in the text undermines.

choiceExplanations.A: is also incorrect because the passage does not shift into a discussion of survey methodology.
choiceExplanations.B: is incorrect because the sentence says nothing about participant selection.
choiceExplanations.C: is incorrect because the underlined portion is not itself a counterexample; the evidence that challenges the proposed explanation comes afterward.
choiceExplanations.D: The underlined sentence offers unequal access to libraries as a plausible explanation for the difference in library use. The next sentence then provides evidence against that explanation: respondents in the city with lower library use were actually more likely to live near a branch. Thus, A correctly describes the underlined portion as presenting an explanation that the text subsequently undermines.

questions.explanation: The underlined sentence offers unequal access to libraries as a plausible explanation for the difference in library use. The next sentence then provides evidence against that explanation: respondents in the city with lower library use were actually more likely to live near a branch. Thus, A correctly describes the underlined portion as presenting an explanation that the text subsequently undermines.

questions.passage:
The following text is from Emilia Rowe’s 1906 novel The Glass Ledger. Helena Varr, who narrates this portion of the novel, has begun studying the history of musical composition.
The village fiddler, unable to name a single principle of counterpoint, nevertheless knew what interval would make a room fall silent and what turn of melody would set feet moving. The most celebrated theorist could tell me vastly more: he could divide harmony into species, trace a cadence through centuries, and assign each modulation its proper term. Yet when I asked why one arrangement of sounds should awaken grief while another, differing by scarcely a note, left the heart untouched, his classifications reached their limit. I had begun to suspect that the very system intended to open music before me had stopped at its outer gate.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Helena admires the precision of conventional musical scholarship but doubts that its usual methods can answer the deeper question she wants to investigate.
choices.B: Helena concludes that practical musicians understand musical theory more thoroughly than scholars do.
choices.C: Helena initially distrusts formal musical analysis but eventually becomes convinced that classification provides the clearest path to understanding emotional response.
choices.D: Helena believes that the emotional effects of music cannot be studied because listeners respond differently to the same compositions.

choiceExplanations.B: goes too far. The fiddler possesses practical knowledge, but Helena never claims that he understands musical theory more thoroughly than scholars.
choiceExplanations.A: Helena acknowledges what formal scholarship can accomplish: theorists can classify harmony, trace historical developments, and name musical structures. However, she finds that these methods cannot answer her deeper question about why music produces particular emotional effects.
choiceExplanations.C: reverses the passage’s direction: Helena becomes dissatisfied with the limits of conventional classification rather than persuaded by its adequacy.
choiceExplanations.D: is unsupported because Helena does not claim that emotional effects are impossible to study; instead, she is dissatisfied with the methods currently available to her.

questions.explanation: Helena acknowledges what formal scholarship can accomplish: theorists can classify harmony, trace historical developments, and name musical structures. However, she finds that these methods cannot answer her deeper question about why music produces particular emotional effects.

questions.passage: Although the Tavira Manuscript Archive in southern Portugal holds far fewer documents than the national collections in Lisbon or Madrid, its narrow geographic focus allows researchers to track commercial practices that were ______ the western Algarve, including rapidly changing credit arrangements used by fishing cooperatives and salt merchants.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: incidental to
choices.B: particular to
choices.C: prohibitive in
choices.D: invariant across

choiceExplanations.C: “prohibitive in,” means excessively costly or restrictive within a place and does not fit the sentence’s meaning.
choiceExplanations.A: “incidental to,” would mean merely secondary or loosely connected to the region, which conflicts with the emphasis on locally distinctive practices.
choiceExplanations.B: The passage emphasizes the archive’s local focus and says that this focus allows researchers to examine commercial practices associated specifically with the western Algarve. “Particular to” means characteristic of or specific to something, so C is the most precise choice.
choiceExplanations.D: “invariant across,” would mean unchanged throughout multiple areas, the opposite of the emphasis on practices tied to one particular region.

questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes the archive’s local focus and says that this focus allows researchers to examine commercial practices associated specifically with the western Algarve. “Particular to” means characteristic of or specific to something, so C is the most precise choice.

questions.passage: Who first introduced the expression “thermal island” into urban-climate research? Surprisingly, ______ Its earliest documented appearance is in a memorandum written by municipal engineer Cora Nishimura in 1917.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: it was introduced by an engineer?
choices.B: was it introduced by an engineer.
choices.C: it was introduced by an engineer.
choices.D: wasn’t it introduced by an engineer.

choiceExplanations.A: has correct declarative word order but incorrectly ends the statement with a question mark.
choiceExplanations.B: uses the inverted word order of a direct question, was it introduced, even though this sentence is declarative.
choiceExplanations.C: After the introductory adverb “Surprisingly,” the sentence makes a statement answering the preceding question.
choiceExplanations.D: combines interrogative word order with a period and changes the meaning into a negative question, so it does not fit grammatically or logically.

questions.explanation: After the introductory adverb “Surprisingly,” the sentence makes a statement answering the preceding question.

questions.passage: Marine engineer Samira Okafor has spent more than a decade at the North Atlantic Instrumentation Center, a research facility devoted to autonomous ocean monitoring. ______ Okafor served as systems lead for the center’s Abyss-7 expedition, during which engineers redesigned a deep-sea sampler so that it could preserve microorganisms at ambient pressure immediately after collection.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Nevertheless,
choices.B: Consequently,
choices.C: Conversely,
choices.D: Specifically,

choiceExplanations.B: “Consequently,” signals that the second statement is a result of the first; however, Okafor’s expedition work is presented as an example of her career, not as a consequence of having worked at the center.
choiceExplanations.A: “Nevertheless,” signals a contrast or concession, but the second sentence does not contradict the first.
choiceExplanations.C: “Conversely,” introduces an opposing relationship that is absent here.
choiceExplanations.D: The first sentence gives a broad statement about Okafor’s work at the research center. The second provides one specific example of that work: her role in the Abyss-7 expedition. Therefore, “Specifically,” is the logical transition.

questions.explanation: The first sentence gives a broad statement about Okafor’s work at the research center. The second provides one specific example of that work: her role in the Abyss-7 expedition. Therefore, “Specifically,” is the logical transition.

questions.passage: In manuscript analysis, a fiber whose surface striations run parallel to the long axis of the sheet is classified as longitudinally aligned. In specimen K-17, the striations follow that same orientation. ______ the fibers in K-17 are classified as longitudinally aligned. Specimen M-4, by contrast, has striations that cross the sheet’s long axis and is classified as transversely aligned.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Hence,
choices.B: Next,
choices.C: Nevertheless,
choices.D: In reality,

choiceExplanations.C: signals contrast even though the conclusion follows directly from the preceding information.
choiceExplanations.A: The first two sentences establish a rule and show that specimen K-17 satisfies that rule. The next sentence states the logical consequence: K-17 is classified as longitudinally aligned. “Hence,” meaning therefore, correctly expresses that cause-and-effect relationship.
choiceExplanations.B: merely indicates chronological sequence, but the relationship is logical rather than temporal.
choiceExplanations.D: usually corrects or qualifies a misconception, and no misconception has been introduced.

questions.explanation: The first two sentences establish a rule and show that specimen K-17 satisfies that rule. The next sentence states the logical consequence: K-17 is classified as longitudinally aligned. “Hence,” meaning therefore, correctly expresses that cause-and-effect relationship.

questions.passage: The following text is adapted from Celeste Armand’s 1913 play The Northbound Star. After retiring from a university post in the capital, Dr. Elias Rane moves aboard a coastal research vessel, where his niece Mara assists the crew. Armand portrays Rane as someone struggling to adjust to life at sea, as is evident when ______
questions.question: Which quotation from The Northbound Star most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.A: Rane says to Mara, “Ask Captain Voss whether the tide tables include tomorrow’s predawn current; I should like to see them before supper.”
choices.B: Rane says to Mara, “At the university I had my study, my lectures, and forty years of books within reach. Here the walls pitch under me, my papers slide from the desk, and every bell summons me to some incomprehensible nautical ritual.”
choices.C: Rane says to Captain Voss, “I have spent my life among manuscripts, not engines, so I shall defer to you regarding the repair.”
choices.D: Mara says to Rane, “You complained of the harbor when we arrived, Uncle, but this morning I saw you watching the gulls for nearly an hour.”

choiceExplanations.B: Choice B most directly demonstrates that Rane is having difficulty adapting to life aboard the vessel. He contrasts the familiar stability of his university life with the ship’s movement, his inability to keep his papers in place, and his confusion about shipboard routines. Those details directly support the claim.
choiceExplanations.A: shows Rane taking an interest in tide tables, which could actually suggest that he is adapting to his surroundings.
choiceExplanations.C: establishes that he lacks expertise with engines but does not necessarily indicate difficulty adjusting to life at sea more broadly.
choiceExplanations.D: suggests that his attitude toward his new surroundings may be improving, so it provides weaker support for the claim than B.

questions.explanation:
Choice B most directly demonstrates that Rane is having difficulty adapting to life aboard the vessel. He contrasts the familiar stability of his university life with the ship’s movement, his inability to keep his papers in place, and his confusion about shipboard routines. Those details directly support the claim.
Choice A shows Rane taking an interest in tide tables, which could actually suggest that he is adapting to his surroundings. Choice C establishes that he lacks expertise with engines but does not necessarily indicate difficulty adjusting to life at sea more broadly. Choice D suggests that his attitude toward his new surroundings may be improving, so it provides weaker support for the claim than B.

questions.passage: Some ecological investigations can be completed with relatively modest funding. For instance, researchers estimating the average number of pollinator visits to a flower species may gather enough observations during a single flowering season to answer a narrowly defined question. By contrast, determining whether restored mangrove forests develop the structural complexity of undisturbed forests may require researchers to measure the same sites repeatedly for several decades. Such work demands substantially greater funding because ______
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: observations gathered during one flowering season generally involve fewer individual organisms than mangrove surveys do.
choices.B: measurements from a large number of restored mangrove sites may still be insufficient to determine their average structural complexity.
choices.C: long-term patterns in forest development cannot be established without collecting comparable measurements across many years.
choices.D: short-term studies of pollinators can reveal ecological changes without requiring researchers to make repeated observations.

choiceExplanations.C: The passage contrasts a relatively inexpensive short-term study with a costly longitudinal study intended to determine how restored forests develop over decades. Such a study requires repeated measurements because the researchers are interested in change over a long period. Therefore, C most directly explains why substantial funding is necessary.
choiceExplanations.A: focuses on the number of individual organisms rather than the principal source of expense identified in the passage: the many years of repeated observation.
choiceExplanations.B: concerns sample size across sites, but the passage emphasizes duration, not an inadequacy in the number of sites.
choiceExplanations.D: describes an advantage of some short-term studies but does not directly explain why the long-term mangrove study requires substantially more funding.

questions.explanation: The passage contrasts a relatively inexpensive short-term study with a costly longitudinal study intended to determine how restored forests develop over decades. Such a study requires repeated measurements because the researchers are interested in change over a long period. Therefore, C most directly explains why substantial funding is necessary.

questions.passage: The Chajnantor Plateau in northern Chile hosts several major astronomical facilities. One installation, positioned more than 5,000 meters above sea level, was the subject of a technical profile _____ in Astronomy & Astrophysics in September 2021.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: appeared
choices.B: has appeared
choices.C: appears
choices.D: appearing

choiceExplanations.C: “appears,” likewise supplies a second finite verb where a modifier is required.
choiceExplanations.A: “appeared,” would introduce another finite verb without an appropriate conjunction or relative pronoun, making the sentence ungrammatical.
choiceExplanations.B: “has appeared,” creates the same problem and also introduces an unnecessary present-perfect construction.
choiceExplanations.D: ” The sentence already has its main verb, “was.” Therefore, the blank must introduce a modifying phrase describing “a technical profile.” The participle “appearing” correctly forms the phrase “a technical profile appearing in Astronomy & Astrophysics.”

questions.explanation: ” The sentence already has its main verb, “was.” Therefore, the blank must introduce a modifying phrase describing “a technical profile.” The participle “appearing” correctly forms the phrase “a technical profile appearing in Astronomy & Astrophysics.”

questions.passage: In 1908, chemists isolated a distinctive amino acid from ergot fungus and initially assumed that the compound occurred only in certain fungi. _____ investigators detected the same amino acid in marine algae, although that discovery was not reported until more than five decades later.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Eventually,
choices.B: For example,
choices.C: Specifically,
choices.D: In contrast,

choiceExplanations.D: “In contrast,” would indicate opposition between two ideas, but the primary relationship here is temporal progression.
choiceExplanations.A: The final clause reinforces this chronological relationship by stating that the later finding was not reported until more than five decades afterward.
choiceExplanations.B: “For example,” would suggest that the later discovery merely illustrates the earlier assumption, when it actually overturns that assumption.
choiceExplanations.C: “Specifically,” would introduce a clarification or more precise restatement rather than a later development.

questions.explanation: The final clause reinforces this chronological relationship by stating that the later finding was not reported until more than five decades afterward.

questions.passage: Participants in a survey were asked to rank architectural landmarks they considered especially “visually arresting,” a term the researchers defined as memorable because of unusual form, scale, or ornamentation. The Sydney Opera House and the Lotus Temple both placed among the fifteen highest-ranked structures. _____ neither received a higher overall ranking than Angkor Wat.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Consequently,
choices.B: Nevertheless,
choices.C: For example,
choices.D: In other words,

choiceExplanations.B: Although the Sydney Opera House and Lotus Temple ranked very highly, neither surpassed Angkor Wat. “Nevertheless” appropriately signals that contrast.
choiceExplanations.A: “Consequently,” would indicate that Angkor Wat’s superior ranking resulted from the other structures reaching the top fifteen, which does not make sense.
choiceExplanations.C: “For example,” would introduce an illustration of the preceding statement rather than a contrasting limitation.
choiceExplanations.D: “In other words,” would signal a restatement, but the second sentence adds a distinct comparative fact rather than rephrasing the first.

questions.explanation: Although the Sydney Opera House and Lotus Temple ranked very highly, neither surpassed Angkor Wat. “Nevertheless” appropriately signals that contrast.

questions.passage: Engineers developing protective coatings for geothermal equipment have proposed transferring some coatings currently used in moderate-temperature systems into a high-heat service range extending from 160°C to 240°C. Not every coating, however, appears equally capable of such a transition.
questions.question: Based on the temperature ranges in the table, the coating that seems least suited to a complete shift into the high-heat service range is _____

choices.A: SiloxaGuard T, because its minimum tested temperature of −10°C is the lowest of the four coatings.
choices.B: CeramiFlex Q, because its maximum tested temperature of 158°C approaches but does not reach the high-heat range.
choices.C: AeroShield PX, because its maximum tested temperature of 145°C lies farthest below the lower boundary of the high-heat range.
choices.D: ThermaBond Z, because its minimum tested temperature of 160°C lies within the high-heat range.

choiceExplanations.A: focuses on minimum temperature, which does not indicate inability to function at the proposed higher temperatures.
choiceExplanations.B: identifies another coating whose tested maximum falls short of 160°C, but its 158°C maximum is much closer to the threshold than AeroShield PX’s 145°C maximum.
choiceExplanations.C: The proposed high-heat range begins at 160°C. AeroShield PX has been tested only to 145°C, meaning its known range ends 15°C below that threshold. CeramiFlex Q comes much closer, reaching 158°C, while SiloxaGuard T reaches 190°C and ThermaBond Z begins its tested range at 160°C. AeroShield PX therefore appears least suited to a complete shift into the new range.
choiceExplanations.D: identifies the coating whose tested range already begins exactly at the lower boundary of the high-heat range, so it is not the least suitable.

questions.explanation: The proposed high-heat range begins at 160°C. AeroShield PX has been tested only to 145°C, meaning its known range ends 15°C below that threshold. CeramiFlex Q comes much closer, reaching 158°C, while SiloxaGuard T reaches 190°C and ThermaBond Z begins its tested range at 160°C. AeroShield PX therefore appears least suited to a complete shift into the new range.

questions.passage: Emily Dickinson’s poem “Hope is the thing with feathers,” first published in 1890, develops an extended metaphor in which hope is given the characteristics of a bird. The poem introduces this comparison directly by describing hope as a feathered creature. _____
questions.question: Which quotation from the poem most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.A: “And never stops at all”
choices.B: “That perches in the soul”
choices.C: “And sings the tune without the words”
choices.D: “Hope is the thing with feathers”

choiceExplanations.A: emphasizes hope’s persistence rather than the specific figurative comparison identified in the claim.
choiceExplanations.B: develops the already-established metaphor by locating the birdlike hope in the soul, but it does not itself make the initial comparison as directly.
choiceExplanations.C: continues the metaphor by giving hope another birdlike behavior, singing.
choiceExplanations.D: The claim specifically concerns the moment when Dickinson directly establishes the metaphor by identifying hope with something birdlike. The phrase “the thing with feathers” does exactly that: an abstract concept, hope, is presented as though it were a feathered creature.

questions.explanation: The claim specifically concerns the moment when Dickinson directly establishes the metaphor by identifying hope with something birdlike. The phrase “the thing with feathers” does exactly that: an abstract concept, hope, is presented as though it were a feathered creature.

questions.passage: Urban-planning researcher Elena Marquez surveyed program coordinators, neighborhood organizations, and residents to compare how each group ranked twenty-five possible benefits of neighborhood cooling projects. A city planner reviewing the results concluded that both neighborhood organizations and residents regarded shaded gathering spaces as an especially important benefit.
questions.question: Which choice best describes data in the table that support the city planner’s conclusion?

choices.A: Neighborhood organizations ranked shaded gathering spaces second and residents ranked them third, higher than either group ranked any of the other four benefits shown.
choices.B: Program coordinators ranked shaded gathering spaces lower than residents did.
choices.C: Residents ranked stormwater absorption higher than program coordinators ranked it.
choices.D: Pollinator habitat received a higher ranking from residents than from either of the other two groups.

choiceExplanations.B: is true as a comparison—program coordinators assigned the benefit a rank of 9 while residents assigned it 3—but it does not directly establish that both neighborhood organizations and residents considered the benefit especially important.
choiceExplanations.A: Because a smaller numerical rank indicates greater importance, rankings of 2 and 3 show that neighborhood organizations and residents, respectively, regarded shaded gathering spaces very highly. Moreover, shaded gathering spaces received the highest ranking among the five displayed benefits from both of those groups.
choiceExplanations.C: is false: residents ranked stormwater absorption 9th, while coordinators ranked it 4th, so coordinators ranked it higher.
choiceExplanations.D: is also false because residents gave pollinator habitat a rank of 13, lower than the coordinators’ rank of 3 and neighborhood organizations’ rank of 11.

questions.explanation: Because a smaller numerical rank indicates greater importance, rankings of 2 and 3 show that neighborhood organizations and residents, respectively, regarded shaded gathering spaces very highly. Moreover, shaded gathering spaces received the highest ranking among the five displayed benefits from both of those groups.

table.caption: Rankings of Selected Benefits of Neighborhood Cooling Projects (1 = highest rank; 25 = lowest rank)

questions.passage: Researchers have proposed that unusually slow, evenly spaced musical pulses may reduce physiological arousal in shelter dogs even when the animals have never previously heard a particular composition. In a study, dogs listened on separate occasions to a slow instrumental adagio and to a rapid orchestral march. The researchers monitored heart rate, treating a lower rate during otherwise comparable conditions as evidence of reduced arousal. They concluded that the slow-tempo music had indeed produced a calming effect.
questions.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researchers’ claim?

choices.A: The dogs’ heart rates fluctuated more irregularly during the adagio than during the march.
choices.B: The dogs’ average heart rates were substantially lower while the adagio was playing than while the march was playing.
choices.C: Shelter employees reported that they personally preferred the adagio to the march.
choices.D: Both recordings contained string instruments as well as percussion instruments.

choiceExplanations.C: reports the employees’ preferences, not the dogs’ physiological responses.
choiceExplanations.A: concerns irregularity rather than whether heart rate was lower, so it does not directly support the study’s stated measure of relaxation.
choiceExplanations.B: The researchers explicitly use lower heart rate as their measure of reduced arousal. Therefore, finding substantially lower heart rates during the slow adagio than during the rapid march would provide direct evidence for the claim that the adagio calmed the dogs.
choiceExplanations.D: identifies a similarity between the recordings but provides no evidence about whether either recording reduced arousal.

questions.explanation: The researchers explicitly use lower heart rate as their measure of reduced arousal. Therefore, finding substantially lower heart rates during the slow adagio than during the rapid march would provide direct evidence for the claim that the adagio calmed the dogs.

questions.passage: Bats determine the size and location of obstacles partly by interpreting returning echoes, whose duration and intensity vary with the surfaces producing them. Acoustic simulations by one research team compared three external-ear profiles—narrow, intermediate, and broad—and found that, when long echoes were embedded in heavy background noise, the intermediate profile separated those echoes from the noise more effectively than the narrow profile did. A second team therefore hypothesized that under acoustically noisy conditions, bats with intermediate ear profiles would be more likely than bats with narrow profiles to detect large obstacles that generate long echoes.
questions.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the second research team’s hypothesis?

choices.A: Some intermediate-eared bats collided with obstacles more frequently than other intermediate-eared bats did.
choices.B: In the same type of tunnel, narrow-eared bats collided with slightly more than half of the obstacles presented to them.
choices.C: In a noisy flight tunnel containing large flat obstacles, narrow-eared bats collided with the obstacles significantly more often than intermediate-eared bats did.
choices.D: Intermediate-eared bats successfully avoided more than half of the obstacles in a noisy flight tunnel.

choiceExplanations.A: describes variation within the intermediate-eared group rather than comparing the two ear profiles.
choiceExplanations.B: shows only that narrow-eared bats frequently collide with obstacles; without comparison with intermediate-eared bats, it cannot establish the predicted advantage.
choiceExplanations.C: The hypothesis makes a comparative prediction: intermediate-eared bats should detect large obstacles more effectively than narrow-eared bats under noisy conditions. If narrow-eared bats collide significantly more often than intermediate-eared bats in precisely those conditions, the result directly supports that prediction.
choiceExplanations.D: shows that intermediate-eared bats can avoid many obstacles, but again provides no evidence that they outperform narrow-eared bats.

questions.explanation: The hypothesis makes a comparative prediction: intermediate-eared bats should detect large obstacles more effectively than narrow-eared bats under noisy conditions. If narrow-eared bats collide significantly more often than intermediate-eared bats in precisely those conditions, the result directly supports that prediction.

questions.passage:
Text 1
In a 2019 essay, marine ecologist Laila Esparza argues that field sketching is among the most accessible forms of natural-history documentation. Unlike laboratory techniques that demand specialized instruments or uninterrupted workdays, observational drawing can be practiced with little more than a notebook and pencil. Esparza writes that useful records have been made “on ferry decks, during lunch breaks, and beneath the weak lamps of overnight trains.” In her view, scientifically valuable observations need not depend on a person’s ability to pursue fieldwork as a full-time occupation.
Text 2
Historian of science Malik Narang argued in 2023 that contemporary biological illustration has become increasingly professionalized. Although anyone may theoretically submit work to specialist journals and field guides, successful contributors often undergo years of anatomical training and sustained drawing practice. They may also need prolonged access to museum specimens or research collections, commitments difficult to maintain alongside unrelated full-time employment. Narang therefore contends that financial security indirectly influences who can develop into a professional biological illustrator.
questions.question: Based on the texts, how would Esparza (Text 1) most likely respond to Narang’s argument in Text 2?

choices.A: By arguing that illustrators whose work appears in specialist publications are generally able to support themselves entirely through biological illustration
choices.B: By asserting that people typically maintain unrelated full-time employment principally to finance the anatomical training required for biological illustration
choices.C: By suggesting that people employed in more lucrative scientific specialties are unlikely to produce worthwhile biological illustrations
choices.D: By pointing out that valuable observational work can be produced under circumstances other than the sustained professional conditions emphasized by Narang

choiceExplanations.B: misrepresents the relationship between employment and training; Narang says full-time employment can make professional preparation difficult, not that people take such jobs in order to fund it.
choiceExplanations.A: is unsupported because Esparza says nothing about whether published illustrators can earn their living from illustration.
choiceExplanations.C: introduces a claim about scientists in more profitable fields that neither text makes.
choiceExplanations.D: Esparza’s central claim is that meaningful observational work does not require a full-time professional setting: useful sketches can be produced during brief intervals and with minimal equipment.

questions.explanation: Esparza’s central claim is that meaningful observational work does not require a full-time professional setting: useful sketches can be produced during brief intervals and with minimal equipment.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
Civil engineer Safiya Mourad has designed several experimental pedestrian bridges using lightweight composite materials.
The Arvand Footbridge was completed in 2018 and opened to the public in 2019.
The Arvand Footbridge uses structural steel, basalt-fiber decking, and laminated timber; its deck area is 418 square meters.
The Qamar Footbridge was completed in 2021 and opened to the public that same year.
The Qamar Footbridge uses structural steel, glass-fiber panels, and recycled polymer decking; its deck area is 736 square meters.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the Arvand Footbridge and the Qamar Footbridge. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Although their other materials differ, both the Arvand Footbridge and the Qamar Footbridge incorporate structural steel.
choices.B: Mourad completed the Arvand Footbridge in 2018, whereas the larger Qamar Footbridge was completed three years later.
choices.C: The Arvand Footbridge incorporates basalt-fiber decking and laminated timber, while the Qamar Footbridge incorporates glass-fiber panels and recycled polymer decking.
choices.D: At 736 square meters, the Qamar Footbridge has a substantially larger deck area than the 418-square-meter Arvand Footbridge.

choiceExplanations.A: The goal is to emphasize a similarity, and A does so directly: both bridges use structural steel even though their other materials differ.
choiceExplanations.B: emphasizes differences in completion date and size.
choiceExplanations.C: focuses entirely on contrasting materials.
choiceExplanations.D: likewise emphasizes a difference, specifically the bridges’ deck areas.

questions.explanation: The goal is to emphasize a similarity, and A does so directly: both bridges use structural steel even though their other materials differ.

questions.passage: Built along the edge of a wind-scoured plateau, the low stone screens at Qasr Nahl were designed to keep drifting sand from blocking irrigation channels and storage ____ the reed barriers documented forty kilometers east served a comparable purpose during the same period.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: courtyards,
choices.B: courtyards;
choices.C: courtyards and to
choices.D: courtyards

choiceExplanations.C: produces an ungrammatical construction because “and to the reed barriers ... served” cannot logically or syntactically continue the first clause.
choiceExplanations.A: creates a comma splice by joining the independent clauses with only a comma.
choiceExplanations.B: The text contains two independent clauses: “the low stone screens ... were designed to keep drifting sand from blocking irrigation channels and storage courtyards” and “the reed barriers ... served a comparable purpose.” A semicolon can correctly join two closely related independent clauses, so C is correct.
choiceExplanations.D: creates a run-on sentence by placing two independent clauses together without appropriate punctuation or a coordinating conjunction.

questions.explanation: The text contains two independent clauses: “the low stone screens ... were designed to keep drifting sand from blocking irrigation channels and storage courtyards” and “the reed barriers ... served a comparable purpose.” A semicolon can correctly join two closely related independent clauses, so C is correct.

questions.passage:
The following text is from Mira Venn’s 1928 novel The Bell Foundry.
Jonas leaned toward the frost-clouded window, but the harbor lamps dissolved into pale smears before he could distinguish the departing steamer. Behind him, the station clerk snapped the ledger shut and began stacking tickets with unnecessary force. Though the clerk said nothing, the sharp movements of his hands betrayed his impatience.
questions.question: As used in the text, what does the word “betrayed” most nearly mean?

choices.A: surrendered
choices.B: misled
choices.C: revealed
choices.D: concealed

choiceExplanations.D: “concealed,” means hid, the opposite of what the clerk’s movements do.
choiceExplanations.A: “surrendered,” reflects a different meaning associated with giving something up and does not fit the sentence.
choiceExplanations.B: “misled,” corresponds to the sense of betraying someone through deception, but no deception occurs here.
choiceExplanations.C: The clerk does not verbally express his impatience, but his forceful movements make that feeling apparent. In this context, “betrayed” means revealed or unintentionally showed, making this choice correct.

questions.explanation: The clerk does not verbally express his impatience, but his forceful movements make that feeling apparent. In this context, “betrayed” means revealed or unintentionally showed, making D correct.

questions.passage: Geochemist Hana Watanabe has analyzed more than eleven thousand deep-sea sediment samples and helped refine several widely used dating methods, but to _____ a durable place in the history of a discipline, few things are as effective as being first. Researchers still cite Leandro Vélez, for example, as the first scientist to recover an intact sediment core from beneath the Amundsen Ice Shelf and the first to identify a continuous volcanic-ash sequence there.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: curtail
choices.B: constrain
choices.C: acknowledge
choices.D: secure

choiceExplanations.B: This choice does not satisfy the evidence, wording, or grammatical requirement established by the question.
choiceExplanations.A: “curtail,” means reduce or limit, which contradicts the idea of creating a lasting legacy.
choiceExplanations.C: “acknowledge,” means recognize or admit and does not fit the construction “acknowledge a durable place ... for oneself.” D, “constrain,” means restrict, which is also inconsistent with the passage’s meaning.
choiceExplanations.D: The passage argues that being the first to accomplish something can help a scientist obtain or ensure a lasting place in a field’s history. “Secure” precisely conveys that idea.

questions.explanation: The passage argues that being the first to accomplish something can help a scientist obtain or ensure a lasting place in a field’s history. “Secure” precisely conveys that idea.

questions.passage:
Annual Days Above the Heat-Alert Threshold
In an urban-climate seminar, a student argues that increasing extreme heat between 2006 and 2021 was evident not only in major metropolitan areas such as Port Aurelia and Northbridge but also in smaller municipalities such as Red Mesa and Cedar Vale. The student adds that the smaller municipalities experienced fewer heat-alert days overall, even as conditions worsened over time.
questions.question: Which choice best describes data from the graph that support the student’s claim?

choices.A: Although Red Mesa recorded fewer heat-alert days than Port Aurelia in every year shown, the totals for both places increased substantially from 2006 to 2021.
choices.B: In 2012, Port Aurelia recorded fewer than 30 heat-alert days, whereas Cedar Vale recorded fewer than 10.
choices.C: In 2006, at least one of the municipalities recorded fewer than 10 days above the heat-alert threshold.
choices.D: Port Aurelia recorded fewer than 25 heat-alert days in 2009, while Northbridge recorded fewer than 20.

choiceExplanations.C: provides only a single low value from the beginning of the period and does not establish an upward trend.
choiceExplanations.A: C supports both parts of the student’s claim. Red Mesa, a smaller municipality, consistently experienced fewer heat-alert days than the larger Port Aurelia, yet both locations show substantial increases over the period. This demonstrates that worsening extreme heat affected both types of places while remaining less severe in the smaller municipality.
choiceExplanations.B: compares two values from one year, so it cannot demonstrate worsening conditions over time.
choiceExplanations.D: likewise gives only 2009 values and does not address the long-term increase or the comparison between large and smaller municipalities.

questions.explanation: C supports both parts of the student’s claim. Red Mesa, a smaller municipality, consistently experienced fewer heat-alert days than the larger Port Aurelia, yet both locations show substantial increases over the period. This demonstrates that worsening extreme heat affected both types of places while remaining less severe in the smaller municipality. A provides only a single low value from the beginning of the period and does not establish an upward trend. B compares two values from one year, so it cannot demonstrate worsening conditions over time. D likewise gives only 2009 values and does not address the long-term increase or the comparison between large and smaller municipalities.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
The Scoville scale measures the pungency of peppers in Scoville heat units (SHU), which reflect the concentration of heat-producing capsaicinoids.
Peppers with higher SHU values are generally perceived as hotter than peppers with lower values.
A cascabel pepper may measure approximately 1,700 SHU.
A poblano pepper may measure approximately 2,900 SHU.
A serrano pepper may measure approximately 18,000 SHU.
A habanero pepper may measure approximately 210,000 SHU.
questions.question: The student wants to compare the pungency of the cascabel pepper and the habanero pepper. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The poblano pepper has a higher Scoville rating than the cascabel pepper but a substantially lower rating than the serrano pepper.
choices.B: Because the habanero’s approximately 210,000-SHU rating greatly exceeds the cascabel’s approximately 1,700-SHU rating, the habanero is substantially more pungent.
choices.C: At approximately 18,000 SHU, the serrano pepper is considerably hotter than both the cascabel and poblano peppers.
choices.D: The Scoville scale can be used to order peppers according to the concentration of heat-producing capsaicinoids they contain.

choiceExplanations.D: explains how the scale works without applying it to the two peppers.
choiceExplanations.A: compares the cascabel with other peppers but never compares it with the habanero.
choiceExplanations.B: This choice directly compares the two peppers specified in the goal and correctly uses the scale: the habanero’s much higher SHU value indicates that it is substantially hotter than the cascabel. A compares the cascabel with other peppers but never compares it with the habanero. B explains how the scale works without applying it to the two peppers.
choiceExplanations.C: focuses on the serrano and therefore does not accomplish the requested comparison.

questions.explanation: D directly compares the two peppers specified in the goal and correctly uses the scale: the habanero’s much higher SHU value indicates that it is substantially hotter than the cascabel. A compares the cascabel with other peppers but never compares it with the habanero. B explains how the scale works without applying it to the two peppers. C focuses on the serrano and therefore does not accomplish the requested comparison.

questions.passage: The Vela Seismic Network, which includes forty-two monitoring stations distributed across three islands, _____ ground motions too faint for people at the surface to perceive directly.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: detect
choices.B: have detected
choices.C: detects
choices.D: are detecting

choiceExplanations.B: “have detected,” also uses a plural auxiliary and therefore creates an agreement error.
choiceExplanations.A: “detect,” is plural and does not agree with Network.
choiceExplanations.C: The subject of the sentence is the singular noun “Network.” The intervening relative clause—“which includes forty-two monitoring stations distributed across three islands”—does not change the number of the subject. Therefore, the singular present-tense verb “detects” is required.
choiceExplanations.D: “are detecting,” likewise takes the plural auxiliary are and fails to agree with the singular subject.

questions.explanation: The subject of the sentence is the singular noun “Network.” The intervening relative clause—“which includes forty-two monitoring stations distributed across three islands”—does not change the number of the subject. Therefore, the singular present-tense verb “detects” is required.

questions.passage: Composer Irena Valdés’s Tesserae cycle consists of twelve string quartets written between 1998 and 2017. The seventh quartet, North Window, ends on an unresolved harmonic figure that might seem unusually abrupt if the work is heard in isolation. Yet the eighth quartet, Salt Orchard, opens by completing that same progression, and Valdés uses comparable handoffs between several other neighboring quartets. For this reason, listeners who treat each installment as entirely self-contained may misinterpret some of the cycle’s structural choices. The twelve quartets are better understood as sections of one extended composition, much as a mural cycle can distribute a continuous visual narrative across separate walls.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: North Window and Salt Orchard are structurally more sophisticated than the other ten quartets in the Tesserae cycle.
choices.B: Valdés’s Tesserae cycle has achieved the same critical prestige as the monumental mural cycles whose structure it resembles.
choices.C: Listeners generally prefer the unresolved endings in Tesserae to the more conventional endings found in other string-quartet cycles.
choices.D: Understanding the structural continuity among Valdés’s quartets helps make sense of features that may seem puzzling when the works are considered separately.

choiceExplanations.A: incorrectly elevates two quartets above the others even though the passage says similar structural handoffs occur elsewhere in the cycle.
choiceExplanations.B: introduces a claim about critical prestige that the passage never makes; the mural comparison concerns structure, not reputation.
choiceExplanations.C: makes an unsupported claim about listener preferences.
choiceExplanations.D: The passage argues that seemingly abrupt features, such as the unresolved ending of North Window, become understandable once the twelve quartets are viewed as interconnected parts of a larger composition.

questions.explanation: The passage argues that seemingly abrupt features, such as the unresolved ending of North Window, become understandable once the twelve quartets are viewed as interconnected parts of a larger composition.

questions.passage: Recommendation systems used by large music-streaming services can occasionally introduce listeners to performers with extremely small audiences by placing unfamiliar tracks among songs the listeners already enjoy. Analysts have found that such recommendations do generate streams for little-known regional musicians. However, the systems deliver substantially more recommendations involving artists with extensive catalogs and large existing audiences, in part because those artists supply many more tracks from which the algorithms can select. Therefore, it isn’t surprising that _____
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: artists with extensive catalogs receive more algorithm-generated streams overall than do little-known artists represented by only a few tracks.
choices.B: most little-known regional musicians already appear in the playlists of nearly every listener who uses recommendation systems.
choices.C: artists with extensive catalogs only recently began to outnumber performers who have released relatively few tracks.
choices.D: performers with the largest catalogs and little-known regional musicians are the two groups most likely to disappear from streaming services.

choiceExplanations.A: The passage establishes that recommendation systems can benefit obscure artists but also explains that artists with large catalogs are recommended much more often because there are many more tracks from those artists available for selection.
choiceExplanations.B: is unsupported and conflicts with the description of the musicians as having “extremely small audiences.” Choice C introduces a historical change in the number of artists that the passage never discusses.
choiceExplanations.D: concerns the likelihood that artists will disappear from streaming platforms, which has no connection to the passage’s discussion of recommendation frequency.
choiceExplanations.C: This choice does not satisfy the evidence, wording, or grammatical requirement established by the question.

questions.explanation: The passage establishes that recommendation systems can benefit obscure artists but also explains that artists with large catalogs are recommended much more often because there are many more tracks from those artists available for selection.

questions.passage: Chemist Fritz Haber is frequently associated with Germany’s use of poison gas during World War I, a legacy intensified by his direct involvement in developing chemical weapons. Yet Haber’s scientific career cannot be reduced to that episode. Working with Carl Bosch, he helped establish an industrial method for synthesizing ammonia from atmospheric nitrogen, an achievement that enabled large-scale fertilizer production and transformed twentieth-century agriculture.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Haber’s collaboration with Carl Bosch was more scientifically important than any research Haber conducted independently.
choices.B: Although Haber is strongly associated with a destructive historical episode, that association can obscure the far-reaching importance of another part of his scientific work.
choices.C: Haber’s work on ammonia synthesis eventually caused scientists to abandon the chemical research he conducted during World War I.
choices.D: Haber’s reputation resulted primarily from the actions of other German chemists rather than from his own scientific activities.

choiceExplanations.B: This choice captures the passage’s central contrast. Haber is widely remembered for chemical warfare, but the text emphasizes that this reputation can overshadow another major contribution: the development of ammonia synthesis, which profoundly affected agriculture.
choiceExplanations.A: is too narrow because the passage does not compare Haber’s collaborative and independent work.
choiceExplanations.C: invents a causal relationship between ammonia synthesis and the abandonment of wartime chemistry.
choiceExplanations.D: contradicts the passage, which explicitly connects Haber himself to both chemical weapons research and ammonia synthesis.

questions.explanation:
Choice B captures the passage’s central contrast. Haber is widely remembered for chemical warfare, but the text emphasizes that this reputation can overshadow another major contribution: the development of ammonia synthesis, which profoundly affected agriculture.
Choice A is too narrow because the passage does not compare Haber’s collaborative and independent work. Choice C invents a causal relationship between ammonia synthesis and the abandonment of wartime chemistry. Choice D contradicts the passage, which explicitly connects Haber himself to both chemical weapons research and ammonia synthesis.

questions.passage: Several pharmaceutical firms operate manufacturing plants in Valmera, collectively producing medicines for both domestic use and export. When the activity of these firms is considered as a single industry, its approximate annual output in 2023 _____
questions.question: Which choice uses data from the table to most effectively complete the comparison?

choices.A: exceeded the output of cloud infrastructure services while equaling that of marine engineering and repair.
choices.B: was greater than the output of both cloud infrastructure services and marine engineering and repair.
choices.C: exceeded the output of marine engineering and repair but remained below that of cloud infrastructure services.
choices.D: was lower than the output of either of the other two industries listed.

choiceExplanations.A: reverses the comparison with cloud services and falsely claims equality with marine engineering.
choiceExplanations.B: is incorrect because pharmaceutical manufacturing did not exceed cloud infrastructure services.
choiceExplanations.C: Specialty pharmaceutical manufacturing produced approximately $9.47 billion. That amount is greater than the $6.18 billion generated by marine engineering and repair but less than the $21.64 billion generated by cloud infrastructure services.
choiceExplanations.D: is incorrect because pharmaceutical manufacturing exceeded marine engineering and repair.

questions.explanation: Specialty pharmaceutical manufacturing produced approximately $9.47 billion. That amount is greater than the $6.18 billion generated by marine engineering and repair but less than the $21.64 billion generated by cloud infrastructure services.
